flags.title: CA Tenant Protection Act (AB 1482)
flags.message: California's Tenant Protection Act caps annual rent increases at 5% + CPI (max 10%) and requires just cause for eviction statewide.
action_items: Verify rent increase complies with AB 1482 cap
Check if just cause eviction applies
Note local rent control may provide stronger protections

flags.title: CA Medi-Cal Expansion (All Ages, All Immigration Status)
flags.message: California expanded Medi-Cal to all income-eligible adults regardless of immigration status as of January 2024.
action_items: Check Medi-Cal eligibility regardless of immigration status
Note managed care plan assignment
Verify behavioral health coverage

flags.title: CA CalFresh Expanded Eligibility
flags.message: CalFresh (CA SNAP) uses broad-based categorical eligibility with 200% FPL gross income limit. SSI recipients now eligible (CA transitioned from cash-out).
action_items: Check BBCE eligibility
Note SSI recipients now eligible for CalFresh
Apply through BenefitsCal.com

flags.title: CA Paid Family Leave (PFL)
flags.message: California provides up to 8 weeks of Paid Family Leave at 60-70% of wages through EDD.
action_items: Check PFL eligibility through EDD
Note 8-week duration
Verify employer compliance with CFRA job protection

flags.title: CA DV Firearms Relinquishment
flags.message: California requires firearms relinquishment within 24 hours of a domestic violence restraining order. Gun Violence Restraining Orders (GVROs) also available.
action_items: Verify firearms relinquishment compliance
Consider GVRO if additional protection needed
Document any non-compliance for court

flags.title: CA Tribal TANF Programs
flags.message: California has multiple Tribal TANF programs operated by federally recognized tribes with distinct eligibility criteria.
action_items: Identify specific tribal affiliation
Check tribal TANF eligibility
Note tribal programs may have different time limits and work requirements

flags.title: Involuntary Hold: 5150 Hold (Lanterman-Petris-Short Act)
flags.message: CA involuntary psychiatric hold law: 5150 Hold (Lanterman-Petris-Short Act). Statutory authority: Cal. Welf. & Inst. Code § 5150. Maximum initial hold duration: 72 hours. Legal standard: danger to self/others or gravely disabled. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 72 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Verify physician certification was completed
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in CA retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Document any communication restrictions imposed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in CA: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Confirm continuous monitoring was documented
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: California Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: California Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
